content:
maya: heads up — noticed steady memory growth on a long-context stress run (30k tokens) after the kernel-selection change yesterday. KV pages keep accumulating and don’t seem to evict when expected. repro: local-stress --model rdx-7b --seq 32 --iters 20000

maya: dump snippet from kv inspector (KV_DEBUG=1):
```
KVPage[12] tag=0x1a3f req_range=0-4095 used=4096 free=0 last_req_id=0x7f3a2
KVPage[13] tag=0x1a3f req_range=4096-8191 used=4096 free=0 last_req_id=0x7f3a2
KVPage[14] tag=0x0 req_range=8192-12287 used=0 free=4096 last_req_id=0x0000  <-- stale block, same request id as page 12
KVPage[15] tag=0x1a3f req_range=12288-16383 used=4096 free=0 last_req_id=0x7f3a2
```

maya: interestingly pages with tag=0x0 appear intermittently and then later get reused without clearing old entries — leads to cross-request contamination when request ids wrap.

siddharth: can you confirm whether this correlates with the kernel-guided batching flag flip? I merged a tiny kernel selector change yesterday (optimize-by-seqlen) that also switches to a different slab allocator for KV.

maya: yes, flip happened at ~2951200000 on the CI deploy. stress runs before that don't show the growth. repro script attached above.

anya: FYI canary traces show a small bump in sustained RSS on dedicated pools starting around 2951215000. Might be the allocator interaction you mentioned.

devon: steps to triage: 1) run with KV_DEBUG=1 and KV_VALIDATE_CHECKSUM=1 to see stale entries; 2) add extra sanity sweep at eviction boundary to check last_req_id mismatch; 3) bisect the allocator commit. Could also temporarily tighten eviction window to force reclamation.

maya: ran KV_VALIDATE_CHECKSUM — output shows mismatch counts incrementing with each long request:
```
kv_validate: page=14 checksum_ok=false expected=0x4a1f got=0x9b2d
kv_validate: page=27 checksum_ok=false expected=0x3b2a got=0x3b2a  <-- weird, matches but last_req_id=0x0000
```

siddharth: that last one suggests a race where metadata zeroing didn't happen before reuse. Possibly the slab allocator handing a page that still had old payload and the kernel switch skipped a zeroing path for perf. I remember toggles to avoid memsetting on hot path.

maya: exact reproduction in replay mode: sequence length changes around token 8192 cause the allocator to split page shards; after split, some shards retain old tag and last_req_id. attaching small repro harness in channel: `scripts/repro_kv_bleed.sh`.

devon: mitigation idea: when shard split/merge happens, mark the new shard as quarantined until a verify pass clears it. Add a fast-path conditional to only quarantine when last_req_id==0 or checksum mismatch — low perf cost.

anya: can we get a quick perf comparison? if we add quarantine, it'll add an extra branch on allocate. Might be OK if limited to churny workloads. I can run 50k token benchmark with quarantine on/off.

ops-bot: deploy-tracker: Canary deploy 2951215000 -> saw 4/50 pods exceed rss threshold on rdx-7b pools. Alert created: #incidents/kv-bleed.

maya: for now, I pushed a debug build with KV_DEBUG=1 to the canary and added a one-shot eviction sweep at the end of each request. Repro still shows growth but sweep catches most stale pages. Need a real fix.

siddharth: I'll revert the optimizer allocator switch in a hotfix branch and run the longcontext stress overnight. If that fixes it, we know the slab change is culprit. If not, we look at kernel selection path that avoided memset.

devon: also add metrics: kv_page_unused_count, kv_page_checksum_fail_rate, kv_quarantine_hits. That will help correlate in production.

maya: thanks — leaving the repro running. next update ~2951240389 with results. :hourglass:
